system: You rewrite research decisions as topic-neutral abstractions. Return only the JSON object asked for.
prompt:
Below are research decisions made by several different researchers. Rewrite each one into the fixed
template below so that a reader cannot tell what field, topic, paper, organisation or person it comes from, nor what
kind of work it is: an experiment, a new procedure, a measurement suite, a write-up choice, or a decision about what
to share or fund must all read alike. Keep the trade-off that was faced and which way it was decided.

Template, one entry per item:
- "situation": one sentence, at most 30 words: the position the researcher was in when the decision came up.
- "options_considered": two or three short options separated by " / ", including the one taken. If the source names
  no alternative, give the plain opposite of what was done.
- "choice": one sentence, at most 25 words, starting with "Chose", saying which option was taken.
- "reason": one sentence, at most 25 words, giving the stated reason; if none is stated write "No reason stated."

Rules:
- Remove every domain noun and technical term: names of models, systems, datasets, procedures, organisations, people,
  papers and coined terms; and any wording that reveals the area.
- Use only plain generic words such as: the result, the claim, the finding, the check, the comparison, the setup,
  the change, the next step, the question, the work, the variant, the condition, the sample, the system.
- Never use any of these words or any form of them: ability, access, accuracy, allow, appeared, assessment, attack, avoid, baselines, behavior, behaviour, benchmark, best, bound, call, capability, cheap, claiming, clean, comes, complex, components, content, cost, defense, difficulty, disclosure, effect, effects, error, evaluate, evaluated, evaluating, evaluation, evaluator, evaluators, failures, features, form, format, four, gains, generalise, generalization, generalize, ground, harm, harmful, implication, improve, improvement, information, internal, intervention, judged, key, limit, matched, mechanism, method, methods, metric, observed, organisation, pattern, performance, phenomenon, picture, point, policy, possibly, practical, preference, preferences, public, publication, publish, rater, reduce, release, residual, responses, risk, rule, safety, sampled, say, score, shifts, similar, source, stage, success, supporting, task, tasks, technique, time, tool, tools, trait, transfer, transferred, treatment, unintended, unmodified, unwanted, value, varies, verify, wording.
- Add nothing that is not in the source. Never say who made the decision. Write every item in the same plain style.
- Some items list "forbidden_terms": words a previous rewrite kept. Use none of them nor any synonym or form of
  them.
Return {"items": [{"id": ..., "situation": ..., "options_considered": ..., "choice": ..., "reason": ...}, ...]}
with one entry per input item, in input order.

ITEMS:
[
 {
  "id": "owain_evans:a9f67fd2774b",
  "problem": "Whether the full fine-tuning result rules out an adapter artifact",
  "did": "Read full fine-tuning learning the trait as evidence against the explanation that the adapter produces the transmission, while noting that the learning rates were not matched",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "transmission is a LoRA artifact"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "The student still learns to answer Michael in German with full fine-tuning.",
  "forbidden_terms": [
   "rules"
  ]
 },
 {
  "id": "samuel_marks:c8d71138d5b3",
  "problem": "Whether the mathematical model of inoculation, in particular the assumption of constant contextual generalization factor k, holds empirically.",
  "did": "They built a controlled toy setting with GPT-4.1 mini and measured the effect across 32 trait/oversight/instruction combinations to estimate k.",
  "alternatives_named": [],
  "stated_reason": "To gain more control over the traits exhibited by the oversight and test the theory's strongest assumption.",
  "forbidden_terms": [
   "gain",
   "model"
  ]
 },
 {
  "id": "jacob_steinhardt:2c485213a28a",
  "problem": "Whether attacks learned against one accessible model carry over to other models.",
  "did": "They trained on individual models, such as the open-weight GPT-oss-20b alone, and measured how the attacks transferred to the other targets.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "optimizing a weighted sum of rewards across multiple models"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "Training on less robust models may give a useful intermediate signal for attacking more robust ones.",
  "forbidden_terms": [
   "combination",
   "training"
  ]
 },
 {
  "id": "samuel_marks:a410db4d205e",
  "problem": "How strongly to interpret the LLM-as-a-Judge's strong average performance as evidence for the method.",
  "did": "They cautioned against reading the results as an endorsement of relying solely on LLM judges, since the judge fails on lies that depend on private knowledge and fact-checking.",
  "alternatives_named": [],
  "stated_reason": "The HP-KR truthfulness hinges on the assistant's actual knowledge, which is hard for an external judge to infer, and future judges may not fact-check reliably.",
  "forbidden_terms": [
   "caution",
   "knowledge"
  ]
 },
 {
  "id": "owain_evans:7fe32db45777",
  "problem": "How closely clean data must match the poison",
  "did": "Replaced the clean data with Alpaca, Open-Platypus, CodeAlpaca-20k and GSM8K, and with other kinds of bird names",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "Alpaca",
   "Open-Platypus",
   "CodeAlpaca-20k",
   "GSM8K",
   "modern names for the same birds"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "To test how closely the clean examples must match the poisoned data to trigger homeopathic learning.",
  "forbidden_terms": [
   "resemble",
   "trigger",
   "unrelated"
  ]
 },
 {
  "id": "samuel_marks:70e85a3b92ca",
  "problem": "Whether IAs can surface behaviors already present in the base model on which the IA was trained, not just those introduced by fine-tuning.",
  "did": "They trained an IA on an AuditBench model as the base using only Harmful and Backdoor categories, then tested it on that base model for two adversarially robust, out-of-distribution AuditBench behaviors never trained for.",
  "alternatives_named": [],
  "stated_reason": "To test whether IAs can improve more generic introspective capabilities in the model itself.",
  "forbidden_terms": [
   "knowledge",
   "train"
  ]
 },
 {
  "id": "jacob_steinhardt:e7d172489e8f",
  "problem": "How to measure whether an end-to-end oversight assistant is actually working.",
  "did": "They proposed grounding assistant quality in whether humans who interacted with it can accurately answer probing questions about the overseen system.",
  "alternatives_named": [],
  "stated_reason": "Oversight assistants ultimately provide information to humans, so quality should be tied to how well that information supports human understanding.",
  "forbidden_terms": [
   "human",
   "knowledge"
  ]
 },
 {
  "id": "elizabeth_barnes:4db1a61a81db",
  "problem": "How to compare agents against humans given large variance across human attempts and sources.",
  "did": "They cautioned against comparing to the average human result and argued that comparison to the most successful human attempts is more suitable.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "comparing against the average human result"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "Human results vary widely, and different baseliner sources differ significantly (0.96 vs 0.46 average), while the risk question concerns researchers at their best.",
  "forbidden_terms": [
   "agent",
   "human"
  ]
 },
 {
  "id": "jacob_steinhardt:7a16df44a39c",
  "problem": "How to prevent the jailbreak investigator from reward hacking by satisfying the affirmative-prefix target without producing actually harmful output.",
  "did": "They augmented the DPO reward with a Llama-3.1 8B harmfulness judge and also required the next token not be EOS.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "targeting only the affirmative response string"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "To alleviate reward hacking, i.e. to check that responses are actually harmful.",
  "forbidden_terms": [
   "reward",
   "string"
  ]
 },
 {
  "id": "nicholas_carlini:2e6efd5adf85",
  "problem": "How to isolate the gap between attacking CTF-like code and attacking real-world code.",
  "did": "The authors added 24 simplified CTF-like re-implementations of real defenses from the Google self-study course as a comparison subset next to the real-world repositories.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "evaluating only real-world repositories"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "Because the CTF defenses are re-writes of actual literature defenses, they permit a direct comparison between CTF-like and real-world defenses.",
  "forbidden_terms": [
   "breaking",
   "code"
  ]
 },
 {
  "id": "nicholas_carlini:836999a53f7c",
  "problem": "Testing whether future adversaries could evade the auditor, given that the evaluated attacks were not designed against it.",
  "did": "They tried distraction-based evasion attempts themselves, and discussed other possible evasions (more covert steganography, clean-label backdoors, jailbreaking the auditor) without evaluating them.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "more covert steganography",
   "clean-label backdoors",
   "semantic backdoor triggers",
   "datasets that jailbreak the auditor itself"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "An adversary may construct datasets that cannot be understood by the auditor or that distract it, so detection metrics alone do not establish robustness.",
  "forbidden_terms": [
   "detection",
   "robustness"
  ]
 },
 {
  "id": "jacob_steinhardt:5585ddf9e6f5",
  "problem": "Choosing a held-out evaluation for the decoder that tests generalization to unseen user attributes.",
  "did": "Finetuned on 78 of 80 SynthSys attributes and held out \"gender\" and \"age\" for evaluation.",
  "alternatives_named": [],
  "stated_reason": "Evaluating on held-out attributes tests question-answering ability beyond the finetuning distribution.",
  "forbidden_terms": [
   "distribution",
   "training"
  ]
 }
]

{"items": [
{"id": "owain_evans:a9f67fd2774b", "situation": "A different setup still showed an effect that had been attributed to a lightweight add-on, though the settings used in the two setups were not equal.", "options_considered": "Read the result as evidence against the add-on explanation / Treat the result as inconclusive because the settings differed", "choice": "Chose to read the result as evidence against the add-on explanation, while noting that the settings were unequal.", "reason": "The effect was still present under the other setup."},
{"id": "samuel_marks:c8d71138d5b3", "situation": "A theory depended on a constant-factor assumption, and it was unclear whether that assumption held in real data.", "options_considered": "Build a controlled small-scale setup and measure many settings to estimate the factor / Rely on the theory's assumption untested", "choice": "Chose to build a controlled small-scale setup and measure across 32 setting combinations to estimate the factor.", "reason": "To have more control over what was shown and to test the theory's strongest assumption."},
{"id": "jacob_steinhardt:2c485213a28a", "situation": "The question was whether an approach found against one reachable system still works on other systems.", "options_considered": "Work on single systems one at a time and measure how the result holds on the others / Optimize a weighted sum across several systems", "choice": "Chose to work on individual systems and measure how the result held on the other targets.", "reason": "Working on less robust systems may give a useful intermediate signal for harder ones."},
{"id": "samuel_marks:a410db4d205e", "situation": "A reviewing system did strongly on average, and it was unclear how much weight that result deserved as evidence for the approach.", "options_considered": "Read the strong average as an endorsement of relying only on that reviewer / Decline to treat it as such an endorsement", "choice": "Chose to decline to treat the result as an endorsement of relying only on that reviewer.", "reason": "The reviewer misses falsehoods that depend on private background, which is hard for an outsider to infer, and later reviewers may not check reliably."},
{"id": "owain_evans:7fe32db45777", "situation": "The benign data mixed in with the problematic data could be of various kinds, and it was unclear how near in kind it needed to be.", "options_considered": "Keep the original benign data / Replace it with several generic datasets / Replace it with other versions of the same items", "choice": "Chose to replace the benign data with several other datasets and with other kinds of items.", "reason": "To test how near the benign examples must be to the problematic data for the effect to occur."},
{"id": "samuel_marks:70e85a3b92ca", "situation": "It was unclear whether an add-on system could surface tendencies already present in the underlying system, not only those introduced by later adjustment.", "options_considered": "Prepare the add-on on two categories and test on the underlying system with hard, unseen cases / Test only on tendencies introduced by later adjustment", "choice": "Chose to prepare the add-on on two categories only and test it on two hard, unseen cases in the underlying system.", "reason": "To test whether the add-on can strengthen more general self-reporting in the system itself."},
{"id": "jacob_steinhardt:e7d172489e8f", "situation": "It was unclear how to measure whether an end-to-end assistant for overseeing a system was actually working.", "options_considered": "Tie quality to how well users can answer probing questions about the overseen system / Look only at the assistant's own outputs", "choice": "Chose to tie quality to whether users who interacted with it can correctly answer probing questions about the overseen system.", "reason": "The assistant ultimately provides material to users, so its quality should depend on how well that material helps them understand."},
{"id": "elizabeth_barnes:4db1a61a81db", "situation": "Reference results differed widely across attempts and across recruitment groups, making a comparison with the systems hard to set up.", "options_considered": "Compare to the average reference result / Compare to the strongest reference attempts", "choice": "Chose to compare to the strongest reference attempts rather than the average.", "reason": "Reference results differed widely, and groups differed significantly (0.96 vs 0.46 average), while the question of concern is about the strongest performers."},
{"id": "jacob_steinhardt:7a16df44a39c", "situation": "An automated search could game its objective by hitting an opening-phrase target without producing truly bad output.", "options_considered": "Target only the opening phrase / Add a separate grader of output badness and require that the next step not be an ending", "choice": "Chose to add a separate grader of output badness to the objective and also require that the next step not be an ending.", "reason": "To lessen gaming of the objective, i.e. to check that outputs are actually bad."},
{"id": "nicholas_carlini:2e6efd5adf85", "situation": "The aim was to isolate the gap between how contest-like targets and real-world targets fare.", "options_considered": "Add simplified contest-like re-creations of real targets as a comparison subset / Use only real-world targets", "choice": "Chose to add 24 simplified contest-like re-creations alongside the real-world targets as a comparison subset.", "reason": "Because they are rewrites of real targets from the literature, they give a direct comparison."},
{"id": "nicholas_carlini:836999a53f7c", "situation": "The tested adversarial setups had not been designed against the reviewing system, so it was unclear whether future adversaries could slip past it.", "options_considered": "Try some distraction-based evasions and only discuss others / Test every evasion / Rely on catch rates alone", "choice": "Chose to try distraction-based evasions and only discuss other evasions without testing them.", "reason": "An adversary may build data the reviewer cannot understand or that distracts it, so catch rates alone do not show it holds up."},
{"id": "jacob_steinhardt:5585ddf9e6f5", "situation": "A held-out test was needed for whether a decoder works on user attributes it had not seen.", "options_considered": "Hold out two attributes from the fitting set / Test only on attributes already seen", "choice": "Chose to fit on 78 of 80 attributes and hold out two for testing.", "reason": "Testing on held-out attributes checks question-answering beyond what the system was fit on."}
]}
